Fetch some for us, or just buy them; we can't use our own accounts on the flea market.
sources.6a619e8e5b0bb16d5b09ee17 description:
Well, with the sensors and transmitters repaired, we detected some very low-frequency communications in Ground Zero that match UNTAR's pattern. The frequency and encryption standards are theirs, but they aren't using the official channels.

I admit I rushed the operation too much, and that could completely compromise our work. This time, I'm going to ask you for a quieter task: no PMC kills, I don't want squads looking for their buddies.

Go there and plant an advanced long-range transmitter near the windows of the locked TerraGroup office; the range should be enough to cover the whole area. I left some transmitters in your stash for you.

Also, check if there's anything off with all the UNTAR vehicles parked downtown.

We're counting on you.
sources.6a6695c403c45274988758fe description:
We intercepted communications from UNTAR officers with the transmitter on Ground Zero. They are using frequencies similar to the official ones, probably to mask their tracks.

These bastards talked about a massive weapons stockpile at the EMERCOM base on Woods that is ready for delivery. Since when do they move weapons? Screw it, you're much closer. Go there and get those weapons before they do, let's figure out what this is all about.

Take this injector, you might need it.
sources.6a66ad2a3fb733233d32a26e description:
My God... Well... The cases you brought... they had, like... A LOT OF STUFF.

UNTAR isn't just transporting gear, weapons, and ammo; they are transporting top-tier stuff. I could keep it all, but let's do this:

Those UNTAR idiots, specifically that unbearable guy named Tadeusz, are breathing down our necks. I don't think they liked that I completely ignored their request to leave Tarkov, and now they're pressuring us.

I told him we are handling some humanitarian matters and said you are helping. I'll give you a bit of what was in those cases. You do some tasks for him while we investigate, and later I'll give you a few more gifts, how about that?

Hurry up.
sources.6a67dba824293fdf6e9ba83e description:
You bought us enough time. Thank you! We made a bet and it was spot on. We wanted to see if any BEAR Operator or Russian authority got suspicious of this, so we started digging through all our informants in enemy territory and counter-intelligence, and bingo!

An FSB agent and a BEAR operator investigated a guy they call "The Supervisor" together, a UNTAR officer in charge of one of the evacuation gates.

The records we have say they stopped somewhere in the offices at Factory, and haven't been seen since.

Turn that place upside down, but find something.
sources.6a680e36dc45fd15657209c2 description:
If there is one truth in Tarkov, it is that despite what the authorities and UNTAR say, Tarkov is no longer under control. For all these years, the world believed this was a war for survival. Fools.

There are PMCs, civilians, and a lot of people who just want to get out of this hellhole, and we will make sure that happens. But for those who found in Tarkov a place merely to cause chaos, profit, and have fun with the destruction... that is ending soon!

I've received dozens more calls from UNTAR officers and haven't answered a single one because this will be the final blow before we prepare to expose every single one of their lies. My people prepared a high-frequency broadcast in multiple languages; we will broadcast for an entire day on all types of radios across Tarkov, warning everyone to stay in their hideouts. We'll prepare various humanitarian operations with supplies and medics.

Whoever leaves their respective bases, we know what they're looking for. More conflict, more war, and not survival, and everyone who steps out will fall, one by one.

Plant another long-range transmitter on the radio tower on Shoreline; my engineers will do the rest. After that, I need you to repair the tower on Woods; it will be enough to amplify the range across all of Tarkov.

See you later!
sources.6a68172d4c48714815c5bcb8 description:
The strike begins now, and we'll see them bleed a little. UNTAR wants us out of Tarkov, right? Then let's show them how humanitarian aid is really done.

We're going to send several operators to deliver supplies in various areas to civilian refugees, non-combatant PMCs, and anyone else who doesn't want to live in this chaos anymore.

At the same time, we'll launch some flares so UNTAR can drop their airdrops. Let's see who is more effective.

We have all our personnel handling the medical supplies. Get us some food provisions and we'll get started.
sources.6a6930180b052dcd27aa3b7c description:
The time has finally come. The broadcast has been looping for an entire day. Anyone operating in any location is to be considered hostile and neutralized. Just don't forget to look out for our friends.

You have done a great job since our first conversation. Although you are not in any of my squads, you are invited to join in, and you will be rewarded in the end.

Today will go down in Tarkov's history, and together we will rewrite its destiny.
sources.690e2689cbd10f2ac5e766eb description: I heard you're looking for information about some people. They are led by an extremely dangerous woman; her operations put Tarkov and everyone involved at risk. Don't hand this over to anyone but me.
sources.c3dd45d0da2679c60db3c3cb description: Maybe you've already heard of this ISB. Well, their leader is pretty... pragmatic. Anyway, maybe giving you a little nudge and helping you connect with her could be beneficial—are you interested? Why not chip in a little?
sources.690bcb580b8f9c461c3eae53 description:
Hello, mercenary! Mechanic trusts you, and so will I. Did you know there is a USEC special operations division? Recently, they've been becoming somewhat present in Tarkov with small operations. 

I've heard rumors that they are working to end this conflict once and for all, and I can't wait for it to be over. So, I've been tracking some footsteps, and they led me to Factory. 

I learned that during a mission in Factory, they were heavily pressured by Scavs and left behind a folder with important documents. I want you to go there, find this folder, and bring it to me. 

Good luck!
sources.690d8ad1750d535b2e9bc135 description:
Hello again, mercenary! It's great to see you're still in one piece. The information in the folder you brought contains data from a TerraGroup investigation, along with USEC, about a secret task force that was interfering with both their operations. A third enemy, or do they have no idea about their own internal resources? 

Either way, the information also says that a document with the possible contacts of the members of this task force was forgotten in the Lighthouse chalet, perhaps that is what those soldiers didn't want us to discover. 

Go there, find the diary, and bring it to me. We need to know who we are dealing with.
sources.690bb986148ac0cfb2669d32 description:
The diary wasn't necessary in the end. I hate having my peace disturbed, but messing with these guys did exactly that. A woman and some soldiers found me and came to talk to me. The woman specifically was impressed with all our effort to establish contact and agreed to talk to us. 

Her name is Aishi, and I feel something strange; it's better to be careful, so keep your eyes open. 

Good luck, mercenary!
sources.690a531eee4e5b9753c9e1f5 description: I know, she seems tough. The truth is, based on what my research shows, she’s part of a special USEC unit, and to this day, everyone in it remains loyal to her. Maybe she’s not used to the way mercenaries operate. In any case, I’ll act as a go-between and show her that you’re worth it—just give me a few good items to use as bargaining chips with her.
sources.690f6e1e9e966ad660423991 description: She is satisfied with your previous performance. I have a few leftover orders from her; find the equipment and bring it. Don't forget to test it; they are very fresh and require fully functional weapons.
sources.69a9df0ea81c67206b147080 description: Hmm, if I know anything about what happened at Lighthouse? Some ISB operators already asked me that. I hope everyone is okay, but unfortunately, I know as much as you do. Keep me updated if you hear anything new.
sources.690a239a90debae535eb1ac3 description: Jaeger connected you with someone who has no idea what they might cause. She sent you to interfere with my things. I trusted you with a task, and you acted behind my back, so you are going to fix this by installing some signal disruptors on the pillars beneath the offices. One on each end and one in the middle should be enough.
sources.69116657e03993e509cc307a description:
Jaeger played a fundamental role in aligning my interests with Aishi's, and I think both she and I can benefit from certain jobs, as long as she doesn't keep interfering with what I do. 

Her team ordered new personalized equipment. I need you to find it for me. I will make some modifications to them so they better suit the purposes.
sources.691240a442a8c7334f0aa46e description: Hello, mercenary. The last modifications were great. I had to replace some of the original parts you brought, but everything went as planned. We have a second batch of orders.
sources.691242e82f0f4e08fcbcd657 description: Hello again, mercenary! Aishi and her people are quite satisfied with our work so far. We are working on a project for her Special Forces, and I hope you can bring me some more equipment. It needs to be of excellent quality.
sources.69667e55c24001ace1f3b128 description: Hey, mercenary! Aishi told me you were coming. So this is the container? It looks like an Alpha-1 model container—a very unusual and rare find. Every time I’ve seen one of these, it was in TerraGroup’s possession, but it really does seem to have some papers inside. There are some security mechanisms, like the ink-based ones found in some banks to self-destruct documents, so it’s best for us to get a better understanding of what this container is and what’s inside it before we try to open it. I’ll do my best to figure out and investigate as much as I can. That’s your job.
sources.6a3cb815f609da9f045ce5df description:
Hello, mercenary. Aishi informed me that you need some information from TerraGroup. Well, according to her report, there is a server block that has already been compromised. It seems to be the last server block near the employee breakroom. So, just plant a Flash Drive in that block and retrieve it after the download is complete.

Good luck!
sources.6a3cc68cf7263a67e12db4ac description: Hello again! My system reports that the download is complete. However, since the information is encrypted, I don't have remote access to it. Head back to The Lab and grab the Flash Drive. Good luck!
sources.69a9e0c6feecd672795d259b description: An explosion at Lighthouse? I hadn't heard about it, but it's certainly not very common to get explosives around here. That's definitely the work of those damn Scavs.
sources.69a9e13ce82619b85edf32ed description: Explosives? Lighthouse? That's not my problem, and I don't even want to get involved with those Rogues. Now, please, I need to focus on my business.
sources.69aa071620304e3c448378fc description: That's not very common in Tarkov, did anyone get hurt? Well, I'd like to help if I could, but I don't know anything. I hope you find the answers you're looking for, mercenary!
sources.69a9e3cfe2ad4cc47d96cf22 description:
Hello, mercenary. It's been a while, how have you been? Hmm... I see, you came all the way here to ask about what happened at Lighthouse. How would you react to knowing that you are the first person to seek me out because of it? Can you imagine why?

Many in Tarkov try to be discreet, and I won't lie to you. It's strange for you, as a good friend, to come talk about this after reports of people dressed in black carrying out coordinated attacks across all locations, eliminating associates... friends, soldiers...

You didn't come here on your own. Hand this over to whoever sent you, and they'll know what to do.
sources.69b44c601144e4b33bdb9e9c description: I knew you'd be back! That wasn't enough, was it? So, let's get down to business! We need to replace the batteries for some of the armored vehicles we have here in the arenas. Depending on your progress, I'll decide what we do next.
sources.69b59f5cd76c01b7117e2712 description: Did your bosses accept the terms? Then we have a deal. 50 million, no more, no less—and I guarantee you'll find out something very interesting.
sources.69a9e71f596a6d5cc7ad6cd8 description: Hey comrade, how's it going? You know how business is, there are things we hear around, but they're more complicated than they seem, so I really can't help you with this Lighthouse thing.
sources.69a9e73c8c336aa789e26a12 description: Hello, Mercenary. It's great to see you in one piece. I haven't received any orders for medical supplies or casualty reports. Did this explosion actually hit anyone? Well, either way, I don't know anything that could be useful to you. I'm sorry. And if you need meds, come find me.
sources.6924bcbfcb0c0c86b8f1aff6 description: Complete a classified operation in line with ISB's objectives for the first time.
sources.6924c9c60db281e82adaf1df description: Uncover and explore the intentions of those who orchestrate the chaos in Tarkov behind the scenes.
sources.694178105154d75f7a0cfd10 description: Embrace your destiny by working alongside the ISB to dismantle and destroy all the corruption plaguing Tarkov
sources.6941763c6b2e0c64d04ef254 description: Locate and neutralize ISB operatives carrying Pawn dogtags (Regular Operatives, Heavy Operatives and Marksman) 50 times.
sources.69417646c9c13c9353996c4e description: Locate and neutralize ISB operatives carrying Pawn dogtags (Regular Operatives, Heavy Operatives and Marksman) 150 times.
sources.6941764b021c3b1630cf28d5 description: Locate and neutralize ISB operatives carrying Pawn dogtags (Regular Operatives, Heavy Operatives and Marksman) 300 times.
sources.694176509df5de06f529631f description: Dive into the corruption of the world and uncover UNTAR’s ties to TerraGroup.
sources.694176555b56f8b3181945b1 description: Investigate and uncover UNTAR’s covert operations on behalf of TerraGroup and Unheard, and get ready to expose them.
sources.694178a7bdec6f74d1f3585a description: Use all the evidence and overcome the pressure from the United Nations in favor of the ISB.
sources.694bf54ab3c3a56da952d2f4 description: Find out about a secret player in the power play in Tarkov
sources.694bf5aefeed87068122e731 description: Find out all the operational details about the Black Division in Tarkov and the evidence they’re trying to hide.
sources.694bf5bc5b0d85dce4d4a3c5 description: Triumphe with ISB and completely dismantle Black Division’s operations in Tarkov while you wait for their final breath at Terminal.
sources.6a6acfb64d8f7b3935a30e22 description:
Hello, soldier! I heard you're trying to get a friend out of a tight spot. Jaeger told me a bit, though he didn't go into much detail.

I plan to send some of my men to Ground Zero. They'll take a look at whatever was left behind and see if they find anything useful. But obviously, I won't send them in while the area is still swarming with Scavs and PMCs, right?

I want you to clear the area before we send the team in. Take care of anyone who might interfere with the operation and let me know when you're done.

Good luck, soldier.
sources.6a6ad307b056d89f85a30e2f description:
Hey there, soldier!

My people scoured that TerraGroup building in Ground Zero and found some interesting things. Nothing that seems very important to your situation, so I'll probably sell most of it.

But they also found a clue that might interest you. Apparently, an unidentified group was guarding documents belonging to someone in a bunker near the bridge on Woods.

Maybe it's the stuff you're looking for. Considering everything we know so far, this is probably our best lead.

Head over there, take a look in the bunker and see what you can find. Let me know when you're done, soldier.
sources.6a6bf9b4e9edcd20cefd27ad description:
Feeling alright?

We got everything sorted out pretty fast, don't you think? But listen, getting involved with a USEC isn't exactly cheap. There are too many people paying attention to this, and I don't intend to put my people at risk without some guarantee.

How about a contribution to cover the operation's costs? And just to be clear, I don't want my name involved in this.
sources.6a6aa8e25ce77038f78f5360 description:
You know, sometimes I get bored watching my people's bodycams and whatever network is still up in Tarkov, and I decide to hack into any vulnerability just to see what's going on.

Do you know Lotus? She's a big trader here in Tarkov, and she has a lot of people too. From the data we have on her, she's more connected to Russia as a whole, RUAF, and their allies.

Well, that doesn't matter much right now. What matters is that I intercepted some signals, and it seems a few Raiders managed to eavesdrop on a broadcast from Lotus to some of her mercenaries. That ended up leaking the location of one of her stashes on Woods.

Even if I offered help, she'd hardly accept it. So head over to Reserve and plant some Jammers on those two main antennas near the tents and the helicopter. That will make them stop listening in on other people's conversations.
sources.6a6ab405957e20e3ed0af439 description: Now that those shits have stopped eavesdropping on other people's conversations, let's teach them a lesson, ISB style. Find some Raiders and wipe them off the map.
sources.6a6be0db93f4ebb01828169d description:
An investigation in record time. Why didn't you tell me sooner? Well, I guess in a way this was payback for that business involving the Raiders.

Anyway, it seems you guys really got me out of a tight spot, not that it makes much of a difference because I'm going to hunt these shits down to the very last second.

Take this, pay Lotus, and keep the change.
sources.6a6abb99edf7cc26c835638a description:
Your friend Aishi is falling into a funnel. If you or she think this ISB will remain hidden, you'd better think again.

Recently, one of my guys managed to get into The Lab; he took a picture of a document he found in the administration room in the main offices and showed it to me. I think you'd better go see it with your own eyes... if it's still there.

Hand the document over to Jaeger when you find it.
sources.6a6abd124b41bb872e356393 description: I already know... Honestly, I almost never have contact with this sort of Federation Fence created. These Scavs just cause headaches, but if it involves Aishi, we'll take a look.
sources.6a6ac726864c233c4ea30e11 description:
Partisan is back. He reported that recently there have been several strange movements in TerraGroup facilities, mainly in Ground Zero and The Lab itself at the Streets of Tarkov entrance.

A lot of documents were left behind, and I know someone who has some very good employees when it comes to researching and gathering intel.

Work with Lotus for a bit, and who knows, maybe she'll consider our position.
sources.66885a3d0221bbe5f306b68d description: Alright, this is a tough request we got in. It's probably best to bring a big ass backpack and get it all done at one time. It's not easy getting in and out of the Labs. You might have to wear one of the armours and shove the other two in your bag. Hide them on the pallet just outside of the hangar gate and dip out - you'll be exposed on your way out. Remember, the armour needs to be in good condition. Don't get it all shredded first.
sources.5f369eeac01a188bc7dc06d0 description: Well, you've been with me for a while in these operations, so let's do the following. I can guarantee that you won't be targeted by my people during raids, but let's practice your role within the "ISB". Deal?
sources.935421a346e854a6d2337c37 description: Currently, my network relies on the highly useful participation of Mechanic and Jaeger. I need to make sure you don't disappoint them either; after all, you want my trust? You need to have theirs too.
sources.f999ba37e8dda410954c0c1f description: Let's see if you can handle placing yourself in the crosshairs of an impeccable aim. By now, you must know Lightkeeper. He frequently annoys me, so how about we send him a delicate warning? Take out one of his trusted sniper's guards, but do not hurt him or any other guards. This is just a warning.
sources.4660ba9168903321ed40bfee description: During firefights, it's very difficult to tell friend from foe, and I want to see if you are up for it. My people frequently conduct operations on Lighthouse and in The Lab. Do a few raids in those locations without hurting any ISB operatives.
sources.ba02d1c72f3ca4c5d6625bf2 description: You did your part. This radio can be used to broadcast your presence in the area. My people will not consider you hostile while you are using it.
sources.6a8f758e89e9b37443ceab22 description: This so-called "ISB" has started moving dangerously. They are scouring large TerraGroup areas in search of documents. We don't know their intentions, but it seems they are carrying highly important material. Whatever it is, I want it for myself. Hold them off while my people grab everything.
sources.0ca9dfa7d14d42f2bd5acdb0 description:
Hello, mercenary! Mechanic informed me that you went through The Lab and witnessed this chaos. You must be confused, and I guarantee I am too. The only thing we know is that an unknown mercenary group is carrying a lot of highly dangerous chemicals.

Their resistance is impeccable, we've never seen anything like it. We need help immediately to hold back the advance of these enemies.

Thank you!
sources.db3b1511110c41cdbab6d4f6 description: We are trying to identify who these Operatives are. Most of my people can't leave The Lab often because they are trying to protect the chemicals. Get some materials and gear from these idiots and bring them to me, so we can see what we're dealing with.
sources.8b708ff6d7e641e38f6f2be0 description: These guys aren't messing around. The only thing we've managed to find so far is an acronym: "BD". Some of my Operatives reported seeing them stash some electronics in their pockets during combat. They also saw one of them locking down a laptop. I need their devices as soon as possible.
sources.8367ca4830984afeb8551aaa description:
The news is terrible. We couldn't break the encryption on most of the intel, but we managed to track the main objective of these idiots.

TerraGroup was researching and conducting experiments with various diseases and genetic modifications in animals. They are trying to recover all the material and research left behind in The Lab. If this falls into the wrong hands, we will have a global catastrophe. Do not let them leave with these materials.
sources.5387285ba1624dab9ac06d72 description:
Our radio taps and intercepts indicated that a codename was repeated several times during the clashes in The Lab: "Wedge". He seems to be leading this whole thing. Look for something that breaks the pattern, like a lot of soldiers protecting him, different gear, and a distinct appearance. These guys like to show off.

Find "Wedge". Neutralize him and bring his items to me.
sources.0b69f84d68d74db7b5dea117 description: Many of the items we need to find are locked in the rooms, and without power in the complex, we'll never be able to access them. Give the keycard readers a little electrical jump-start; that should be enough to get in with an access card.
sources.a3f407eb22cd41769e6f4c5f description: Here's something not even we at the ISB were aware of, and we know TerraGroup top to bottom. C.A.S.S.I.E. is a system called "Central Autonomic Service System for Internal Emergencies" that monitors extremely high-level risks in TerraGroup facilities and automatically arms defense measures—a cutting-edge AI. We need access to it and its operational details before this robot pulls a stunt impossible to fix. Neutralize these Black Division shits and find some useful intel that helps us understand this system.
sources.52588eccea984354a13b53f4 description: I don't care about Skier's clients. What is happening in The Lab is far too serious for us to care about that. Take out those Raiders and PMCs that are causing trouble and that should settle it.
sources.1184c00a9ec847be987be767 description: It's quite audacious for this madman to want to mess with my "White Tusks". Ignore this nonsense and keep helping with the research against these mercenaries. We need to find out more about them.
sources.cd993bfe6ed447dcaab85d04 description: Peacekeeper thinks that turning a blind eye to these unknown mercenaries will save him from being exposed? It definitely won't! Ensure the safety of the ISB teams in The Lab by eliminating a few more of these operators. Don't you dare get in the way, mercenary!
sources.8e039d03e80f41788f9b9819 description: This “ISB” has an extremely skilled squad called “White Tusks.” I don't care what they do at Labs, but I don't want them causing trouble outside of it. Deal with them.
sources.66a3c03136254144b3cf9e93 description: Your "ISB" friends fell into quite a trap. No matter the outcome of this conflict, the Black Division got what they wanted. They exposed the great "super secret USEC unit" and will slip into the shadows themselves as usual. I'm interested in how this will all end. If you want me to try and interfere with Black Division's damage, get me "ISB" documents.
sources.55ccb3bc5af1428fb03001df description: I am aware of what is happening in The Lab. This is a great opportunity to learn how to get out of difficult situations. I trust you and I know everything will be fine. Complete Aishi's tasks and get out of there in one piece.
sources.dd715e78ab984c14909da407 description:
Hello, mercenary. Aishi sent me some reports of what is happening in The Lab, and to sum it up for you: total chaos.

If you are here, I imagine you want to help, so go to the lab and do some recon.
sources.f1a90496778649e8b955e60d description: The entire electrical system in The Lab is a mess. Gates are locked, elevators shutting down... Everything is alarming. Go to the security area near the research lab and access the Alarm and Emergency Lights controls. For you to get out of this place, you'll have to activate the emergency pistons for the 2 gates. Each of the pistons is located near their respective control centers. After that, go back to the server and activate the gates' security system. That will open them for you to get out.
sources.a38b841cae6d46dab703e8eb description: My analysis says The Lab's auxiliary power system is still intact, but with the whole system damaged we'll have to manually activate the power cells. Confirm if the first power cell is working in the Main Generator room. It's located near one of the main elevators.
sources.c9304d1a70414b398f840595 description: I managed to locate each of the auxiliary power cell generators. To restore power to the facility you need to reactivate each one of them. Besides that, the rooms' Keycard readers are off, you'll probably need a temporary power source like a GreenBat Battery, that should do.
sources.9dfc181b7e2944bd9d40308b description: While I work on the structural part of the lab and the systems, help Aishi with her tasks. It is also possible that other traders might be interested.
sources.a5933b154fe34593947956c8 description: This "ISB" always gives me a headache. Mercenary, are you seeing what they are doing in The Lab? Neutralize some of their commanders for me, that will help disorganize the squad.
sources.688a35cea49a4833a17c74b0 description:
Hello friend! Did you see what is happening in The Lab? I heard everything there is literally on fire. Well, I found out from some sources that a new faction, the "ISB", is present there along with some other unknown mercenaries.

You know how it is, right? These new guys always use really cool gear and my clients would love it. Get some for me!
sources.85baf5fc8723406a88b049a5 description: Hey Mercenary! How are you? You know how it is, some of my clients are Raiders or have contact with them, and I heard a new crew, some "ISB", is causing chaos in The Lab along with some other unknowns. This makes business difficult. Clear the area for me so my people can grab some things.
sources.1f6a892b5dda4241868ffd09 description: Looks like that crazy place is suffocating everyone after a while. Respirators aren't enough to save you, but they delay total oxygen loss. Get some for me.
sources.e4e78f48c1e44d898e8ad5e3 description: I heard some soldiers from another group are operating in The Lab and they informed me they have some very powerful stimulants. I would like to study some of them. If you can, when you drop by The Lab, bring some to me.
sources.64e6df2f30554b3ea6e4e1c9 description: Records indicate that a group of unknown mercenaries is transporting many infected biological materials in The Lab. Specifically, a virus project that I understand a bit about. If this is not handled properly, it could become a global problem. Please, mercenary. Get some samples for me.
sources.35dc82a3c84b4c0a8a0646d8 description: Mechanic contacted me. We found out that this C.A.S.S.I.E. system is fully automated to handle crises. Not even our adversaries are controlling it, and this could cause catastrophic problems for our operation. I've prepared a quite fun countermeasure for this, but it seems we'll need some of our opponents' equipment. Their encryption data is very useful against C.A.S.S.I.E. Assemble our device and let's move on.
sources.10413f0d043844c6a69a88db description:
With the system virus ready, we can move forward. It seems the system operates with two passwords. The first is the general research manager's password, and we are trying to crack it and contact the scientist around the clock. The second password, C.A.S.S.I.E. sends automatically when an emergency is detected.

Place the modified flash drive with the virus in the lower server wing, then look for the main office; that might help expose the password!
sources.637a389d84da48a4a34dfd17 description: It seems the administrator's room uses a fully isolated electrical system. Without power, you'll need a much more sensitive battery to deal with that reader. I sent you some blueprints to build it. Just don't forget the toolset. Enter the room and access the terminal.
sources.b8432fd547b146bfa8b77dd6 description: With the data terminal under control, we can access all recent research and control C.A.S.S.I.E.'s decontamination systems. Bring me this data and disable that system once and for all; we can't afford to lose more personnel.
sources.8e4f5535e0bf4135b8a90ec7 description: You managed to extract all the data? Great! With it, we can put an end to this sick TerraGroup experiment once and for all and prepare for any eventuality.
sources.ca7b2ef7bca84efe967f9b40 description:
Hello mercenary! Aishi and I are trying to understand how this C.A.S.S.I.E. system works. She knows a lot about systems, way more than I imagined. Well, anyway, all ISB personnel are busy holding the line in the facility, so I need you to restore part of the system so I can access the files.

Reactivate the facility's power and plant a device in the server blocks—specifically one near some boxes on the floor; it's more vulnerable. After that, just get out of there!
sources.a3b3fae920584af7b941a2fc description:
Hello, soldier! How's it going?

It seems that "ISB" woman got herself into a big mess. Jaeger updated me a bit on the situation, and it looks like several highly dangerous chemicals are almost spiraling out of control.

Some unknown mercenaries are carrying special antidotes, and they could be very effective for some research. Get me a few of them, and I can help with this whole containment effort.
sources.6e49a30eafa8409bbf623897 description:
Hello again!

I sent some of my people to do recon in The Lab, and I really don't know how you're handling all of this so easily. Well, some TerraGroup documents are quite interesting. They were studying not only this virus, but something they call "KTE" (Unknown Threat Entity)—items that somehow possess very strange properties. Hard to believe, isn't it? Well, I want to research some, so bring me a few samples.
sources.6a5d3f64a8b2157267046245 description: Locate and neutralize ISB Special Agents (Team Leaders, Specialists, Scouts and Assassins) 30 times.
sources.6a5d3f7ffc741ffbbf091b8e description: Locate and neutralize ISB Special Agents (Team Leaders, Specialists, Scouts and Assassins) 90 times.
sources.6a5d3f83cfd86f66e72d47a5 description: Locate and neutralize ISB Special Agents (Team Leaders, Specialists, Scouts and Assassins) 150 times.
sources.6a5d422c743a1afbb2183f54 description: Locate and neutralize "The Chosen One" and "The Dark Lord" in a single raid.
sources.6a5d431a5243a4c3a0d2afe9 description: Locate and neutralize "The Chosen One" and "The Dark Lord" 30 times.
sources.1d9f3fb317d15e2a77957327 description: Contribute to the ISB and expel the Black Division forces from The Lab by completing the entire Aishi's quest line for the “Containment Breach” event.
sources.1c69974a9de656678427b103 description: Eliminate each of the seven White Tusks members at least once.
sources.9df3731674b1b81ebec38ce4 description: Survive the decontamination protocol at Labs during the “Containment Breach” event for 10 minutes and extract from the raid.
sources.c447fc786e04524e87d4ea8a description: Overcome the Black Division and obtain information from the C.A.S.S.I.E. system for the ISB during the “Containment Breach” event.
sources.aee00b2dc375dce6a12450d0 description:
You're new. Or new enough. I don't need your rifle or ammunition; I collect information. Proper information. Bring me one PMC tag. BEAR, USEC, I don't care. Read the name before you hand it over. People skip that part. I don't know why. And please, don't clean it.

A tag can tell me where its owner came from, but the interesting part is what happened afterward. Even a scuffed edge can place a person somewhere a tidy official record never will. Start with one, and let me see what your part of Tarkov leaves behind.
sources.ad9c91314a6c311c3ec9cbc7 description:
One specimen tells you very little. I need comparison: one BEAR and one USEC. Differences in issue, manufacture, wear. Names too. I had a Krupa in one pile and another Krupa in a different set of notes. Probably unrelated. Probably. The details matter.

I have two trays on the desk. People keep assuring me the factions are interchangeable once the fighting starts, but their equipment tells a less convenient story. Place one in each tray. I want to look at them side by side before I draw any conclusions.
sources.2ab7e1da342dbdc151803e69 description:
Fresh tags tell me very little. Bring me three from operators level twenty-five or higher. I want people who lasted long enough to learn something. There is a USEC called Lukáš "Forester" Krupa in one of my notes. I keep wondering whether the nickname describes a habit, a place, or merely somebody else's joke. That is the trouble with names. They tell you more and less than numbers at the same time.

You can learn a great deal from somebody who has been here long enough to replace their original kit. Repairs accumulate. Habits become visible. I suspect their tags will show the same thing, though I would prefer evidence to a hunch.
sources.eed4c1f2f4515018fca28da0 description:
I've reorganised the collection and found an irritating gap. Five tags should correct it. Any faction, any level. This one is about filling the space. Although I found myself remembering a man called Miron "Skala" Timofeev while I was moving the trays. I don't remember his number. That seems backwards.

The empty spaces are numbered, which was a sensible system until I began looking at them instead of the objects around them. Now I cannot concentrate. Fill this section and I may finally be able to work on something else.
sources.37ad5422d1ed717a2e87d0ca description:
Four BEAR and two USEC. No, the ratio isn't arbitrary. I have a reason. You don't need the reason. There are surnames that appear on both sides, incidentally. Petrov. Vardanyan. Gasparyan. It complicates things. Faction is supposed to simplify the record, not make me wonder whether two dead men were cousins.

I found the ratio in a report that was more interested in victory than the people involved. The figures ought to be checked against something real. I will explain what I am looking for when I know whether the report was worth keeping.
sources.ec2dcb5e6b514ad343744a2d description:
Four tags, level seventeen or higher. Seventeen is the appropriate threshold. I've done the calculations. No, you can't see them. A man called Daniil "Rebus" Belov survived long enough to appear in three separate scraps of information I was given. Or there were three Belovs. I need better records.

My notes suggest a curious change around that point. Before it, people seem to rely on whatever they were issued. After it, they begin making choices of their own. I want four examples before I decide whether that is a pattern or simply a pleasing story.
sources.d82f1b248a0232e53006ca00 description:
I realised I made a mistake when we first met. I gave you a bottle. I meant to give you the beer. Bring me a bottle of beer back, and seven tags while you're at it. I'll dispose of the contents. Also, if you see the surname Leone, don't discard it. I have several Leones in the notes now. That may mean something, or Italians simply have surnames.

There is a stain on my ledger where I set the original bottle down. It has made a surprisingly persuasive argument for correcting that transaction. The tags are a separate matter, though I may as well record both debts at once.
sources.72362110d1f507767b8aabaf description:
I've got another gap. Nine should do it. Any kind. Read a few of the names before you bring them. I found one listed as John "Tag" Price, which is either an extraordinary coincidence or proof that mercenaries have a worse sense of humour than I thought. Also remind me about the ammunition under the desk. I've stubbed my toe on the box three times.

The box beneath my desk is marked ammunition, but I have not opened it since it arrived. There are several equally mysterious parcels beside it. Help me finish the next row, and you can take the whole obstacle away.
sources.1cdaa539513c7192a52b2f0a description:
I've been approaching this inefficiently. This time bring me fifteen tags, any fifteen. I want volume. No, this doesn't mean I've stopped caring about the details. Quite the opposite. With enough names, the repetitions start to bother you. Families, common surnames, nicknames reused by strangers. Or perhaps I am inventing patterns because blank columns annoy me.

Individual stories can mislead you. Fifteen may be enough to show me which marks occur by chance and which appear again and again. I have cleared a table for them, although I may have underestimated the amount of table required.
sources.c93d221e4b72a43bd8de15d4 description:
Fifteen at once was a mistake. I've been awake most of the night cataloguing them. Bring me proper coffee and five tags level twenty or higher. Also, I think it's my birthday. Approximately. The flea contact who calls himself Night Clerk says birthdays matter. I don't know why I take social advice from a man named Night Clerk.

I have been sorting names into columns all night and twice caught myself writing the same one. That is unacceptable. The coffee is for me; the experienced tags are for the record. If the date written on the wall is correct, this is also an excellent excuse to call the exchange a celebration.
sources.a9071cc02877f30fb09e1118 description:
I want symmetry: five BEAR, five USEC, all level eighteen or higher. Ten total. Nice and balanced. No, eighteen isn't arbitrary. Arkady "Tigr" Rodionov is in my notes twice. I think. One entry says Customs, another says Woods. If it is the same man, he moved around. If it isn't, I have wasted twenty minutes comparing handwriting.

A balanced sample ought to make comparison easier. I want to see whether two groups with similar experience chose different ways to stay alive. Ten records will make a fair beginning. You, meanwhile, should consider taking the medical equipment I have accumulated.
sources.b650c014ce2da9678c4e3880 description:
I've made another mistake. Five and five looks excellent, which apparently makes it statistically unhelpful. I need three BEAR and eight USEC. Uneven samples show different things. So do uneven lives, apparently. One of the names I have is Finlay "Wrongway" Baker. I keep wondering whether the nickname was earned before or after Tarkov.

The last arrangement was tidy enough to frame and almost useless for answering the question. Real evidence rarely presents itself in matching columns. This time I intend to leave the imbalance exactly as it is and see what it tells me.
sources.1d11cbc194a45afe5f8d91cf description:
Disaster. Absolute disaster. I could have sworn there were five here. I need five USEC tags, level twenty-three or higher, as soon as reasonably possible. I have a gap. I also have two entries for men called Leone and one for a "Lion" Leone. I am beginning to resent surnames.

I have checked the shelves, the envelopes and the floor. I was not robbed. I simply wrote down five names before I had five tags. It is an embarrassing error and one I would appreciate resolving before anybody else notices the labels.
sources.96a8d109cd42b725b00320ec description:
Level thirty interests me. By then somebody must have learned something. Bring me ten tags, level thirty or higher. There must be a pattern to survival. Route choice, equipment, patience, aggression, luck. I have a man called Michael "Backtrack" Scott in the notes. Perhaps he understood something useful. Or perhaps he simply got lost often enough to acquire a nickname.

Experience is often treated as proof of good judgment. It may only prove that somebody survived long enough to make more decisions. I want to know whether the older tags share anything beyond their numbers, even if the answer is uncomfortable.
sources.91646996e6ceb4b7f6f75bc9 description:
The last sample was inconclusive. Perhaps faction is the missing variable. Six BEAR, six USEC, all level twenty-four or higher. Same quantity, different training. I have USEC and BEAR records sharing surnames now. Vardanyan. Tsereteli. Mirzoyan. I cannot tell whether that means family, coincidence, or that I am asking the wrong question.

A larger sample failed to explain why some people last and others do not. Training is the next thing to test. Keep the factions separate, but hold the threshold steady. If the results still refuse to cooperate, I will have to admit the question is harder than I thought.
sources.3247908b2e049cb2a4f9ff61 description:
I've noticed something. You're keeping these, aren't you? You're trying to anticipate what I'll ask for before I ask for it. That means you're not looking at them properly when you take them. You're just storing inventory. That isn't what we're doing. I thought this was a study, not a courier service. Bring me forty tags, any faction, any level. Consider it an audit. And this time, read the names. Forty is excessive. That's precisely the point.

You have been glancing at that case every time you come in. I recognise the look; it is the one I used to give my first cabinet. Collections need records and limits. Forty ought to establish whether yours has either.
sources.1f07a929ab26733759f54555 description:
All right. Forty may have been excessive. I was making a point. Possibly too firmly. Three this time, level twenty-one or above. Why twenty-one? Because twenty wouldn't be enough. They're different requirements. I found a note about a trader calling himself Bookkeeper. I dislike the name. It feels competitive.

I reviewed our last exchange and decided that forty may have been a little much. I am not apologising for the audit; the result was informative. This request is smaller, and the payment is considerably better. Make of that what you will.
sources.dd0e8d708283c0aa46ab70b8 description:
Suppose one USEC is alone and four BEAR are closing in. He can't leave; the route behind him is blocked. Bring me one USEC and four BEAR, level fifteen or higher. I want to arrange something. Call the USEC Gabriel "Hollywood" Williams for the moment. A ridiculous name, but a useful marker. If Hollywood survives, I want to know why.

I have drawn the roads and buildings on an old sheet of paper. The isolated man has cover for perhaps a minute before four others can reach him. Different levels of experience would ruin the exercise, so find me people who have at least seen a few fights.
sources.9f48571604b7bad741012db0 description:
I continued the scenario. Hollywood survived. Now six USEC have arrived, and two more BEAR. Bring me six USEC and two BEAR, all level twenty-eight or higher. Please don't mix them together. I know none of these are actually Hollywood. That isn't the point. Or perhaps it is. I'm still deciding.

The first arrangement was too simple. Reinforcements change the lines of sight, the ammunition needed and the temptation to retreat. I have moved the pieces twice already. Bring the next group and I will find out whether my survivor still deserves the name.
sources.06322b8096b190250b040787 description:
There's a problem. Seven BEAR are advancing on three USEC. Their position is defensible, but I've calculated the ammunition expenditure. They didn't bring enough. Level thirty-two or higher. There is a BEAR called Nikita "Strelok" Sukhanov in the records. Strelok means shooter. Useful nickname. Useless information unless I know whether he survived because he could shoot or was called that because he could shoot.

I counted the rounds each defender could carry and then counted the approaches. The sums do not agree. I have three magazines on the table to demonstrate precisely what should have been packed; perhaps that will persuade you to check your own kit before leaving.
sources.36cffca1f19896687dc65992 description:
I've changed the scenario. Four BEAR, four USEC, level twenty-eight or higher. Twenty-eight gives the most useful result. Assume the first plan failed. Now account for bleeding, exhaustion, bad information and panic. People keep treating plans as if failure is an exception. I am beginning to think failure is simply another column.

A plan that only works while everyone behaves as expected is a poor plan. I am adding injuries and a blocked exit to the board. Equal groups will keep the comparison useful. What matters now is whether anyone can adapt quickly enough to leave.
sources.c4a117cee0f216e5f128a018 description:
I've stopped the scenarios for the moment. They weren't producing anything useful. Change enough variables and you can construct any outcome you want. Seven BEAR, nine USEC. No minimum level. Just facts. A contact called Quartermaster says this is how supply works too. I suspect he is trying to sell me something.

I caught myself moving a piece back onto the board because I disliked where it had fallen. That is not analysis. The board is put away. Bring me records with firm numbers, and I will write down what I find without trying to improve the ending.
sources.7e6b06e38ec82a77012b404b description:
There's an error. Six point four percent. Small, but still an error. Six tags, level thirty-three or above. That should correct it. I saw the name Yaroslav "Volk" Konovalov again. Or I think I did. If I start recognising people who are supposed to be random samples, the sample is no longer random. Annoying.

The correction is in a footnote nobody else would read. I read it, of course. Six additional records should bring the totals into line. Whether a better total leads to a better conclusion is a question I intend to postpone until tomorrow.
sources.7823e877629e7dcf22f72331 description:
I want to understand guns. Not what they do. The fascination. Bring me a standard Glock 17 and three tags, level twenty or higher. A man in the flea notes calls himself Gunsmith, which is either reassuringly literal or deeply suspicious. Do not customise the Glock. I want the boring version.

People describe a pistol as if every part were an argument. I would like to see the unaltered object before hearing another opinion about it. The tags provide a familiar control group, if that makes this sudden interest sound more respectable.
sources.2a649124d2a8231fa999b488 description:
I've been experimenting. Not because I'm interested; the Glock simply wasn't representative. Bring me five tags, level nineteen or higher. Then I want your opinion on two rifles. I keep seeing equipment described as if it explains the person carrying it. It doesn't. But perhaps it explains what they expected to happen.

I took the pistol apart, put it back together, and somehow ended up reading about thermal sights. I have prepared two rifles for your inspection. One is meant for close work; the other is built for distance. The comparison may tell me more than another evening with a parts catalogue.
sources.4930760967b54ecbdf0de1c2 description:
I've learned enough about firearms to identify a problem: people have been giving me rubbish. Bring me eight tags, level fifteen or higher. I'm clearing the surplus at the same time. If one of the names happens to be Mitchell "Tiny" Hudson, tell me. No reason. I just want to know whether Tiny was, in fact, tiny. This work is becoming less dignified.

Once people discovered I could identify a weapon, they began leaving unwanted ones here. The pile has occupied the chair where visitors are supposed to sit. Take the lot as payment for the records, and I might remember what the room looked like before this experiment.
sources.9fa096456797de612a502e05 description:
I've stopped studying firearms. Yesterday I spent forty-three minutes comparing two muzzle devices. That's not research, it's an illness. Bring me three BEAR and five USEC, level twenty-two or higher. I'm emptying the attachment drawer. Every piece is different this time. I checked. Twice.

I can tell you exactly which parts would fit the weapons in the other room, and I resent having learned it. The drawer is full of attachments I bought while trying to settle an argument with myself. Please take them before I start another one.
sources.c6ca9c38f4541c085b962f43 description:
Somebody laughed at my computer. It starts, displays information and stores my records; I considered that sufficient. Apparently it isn't. Bring me one graphics card and five tags level twenty-six or higher. There is a USEC called Dev "Sparky" Akhtar in my notes. If he understood computers, I wish he'd left instructions instead of a nickname.

The old machine has my catalogue, correspondence and several years of corrections. Its appearance has never bothered me. Being told it is obsolete has bothered me considerably. Bring the replacement component and I will discover whether the criticism was justified.
sources.30a704732647ff8a8615a745 description:
The graphics card has created a problem. Power, cabling, cooling, compatibility. Every improvement generates three more requirements. Bring me a military cable, a military power filter and six tags level twenty-eight or higher. I have begun to appreciate why the dead are easier to catalogue than computers.

I followed the instructions as far as the word 'install', then discovered that replacing one part apparently requires replacing half the room. The cable and filter are on the list I was given. I have also kept working on the collection while this expensive lesson unfolds.
sources.d3c7160860d97d80ccb9135a description:
I've dismantled the computer. All of it. I'm done. Bring me nine tags. Any kind. Metal, stamped numbers, no drivers, no firmware. A flea trader called Red Ledger offered to buy the old components. I declined on principle. There should not be two Ledgers in one market.

There is a heap of perfectly good machinery on the floor and none of it currently does anything. I will return to paper and metal for a while. At least I understand how to file a tag without somebody asking me to update it first.
sources.3eb264a90ae286106a23c6f7 description:
I've been wondering what these actually represent. A name, number, faction. That's what remains after everything somebody did and knew. Bring me three. I don't think the numbers matter this time. One of the USEC names is Giulio "Duke" Leone. I've seen Leone before. Several times, actually. If Duke is still out there, I would like to know what he keeps doing right.

I used to arrange the tags by faction, level and condition. Last night I read a name aloud to check a spelling and found myself wondering who would recognise it. Choose three without regard to rank. I want to begin recording the people, not merely the specimens.
sources.2348be9a1126aa50393bd717 description:
There's been a minor complication. My records were on the computer. Paper doesn't crash or require drivers. Bring me printer paper, three secure flash drives, and five tags level twenty-five or higher. Yes, I realise asking for flash drives while complaining about computers is inconsistent. The ledger is allowed one contradiction.

My old records contained numbers that looked precise and told me almost nothing about their owners. On paper I can leave room beside each name for a detail or a question. I will copy what I can recover, then start doing the rest differently.
sources.f59a6554361e1943b5757620 description:
Paper was a good idea in principle. I've now written hundreds of names. My hand hurts, my neck hurts, my head hurts. Bring me two packs of painkillers and seven tags level twenty-nine or higher. I wrote 'Duke Leone' in the margin and then found Tommaso "Lion" Leone elsewhere. Different man. Probably. This is exactly the sort of thing that keeps me awake.

Several names now have small notes beside them. One had repaired a clasp with wire. Another had polished the front so often the back looked neglected. None of this fits neatly into a table, which may be why I keep noticing it.
sources.70494923f4313a0836047a56 description:
The light has become unpleasant after several hours of paperwork. Bring me something tinted for my eyes, three packs of painkillers, and six tags level thirty-one or higher. I'm solving a problem, not making a fashion statement. Also, I may have found Duke. No. Wait. Fabrizio Leone. Wrong Leone. Ignore that.

The writing has filled an entire wall, and the desk lamp has become an enemy. I have been offered a key to a room with better light, but I suspect that would create more problems than it solves. The glasses seem a more reasonable experiment.
sources.3a70daa9069403bb0c87aac6 description:
I've been thinking about the locals. Scavs. They don't carry tags, which is inconsiderate, but they carry other things. Bring me cigarettes, two bottles of vodka, and eight tags level thirty-four or higher. Old Vanya says possessions tell you more than paperwork. I have no idea whether Old Vanya is a person, a business, or three scavs sharing a coat.

The locals carry evidence of ordinary days in their pockets: a habit, a meal, something saved for later. I have spent years overlooking it because none of it had a stamped number. Add a few of those things to this week's records so I can see what else I missed.
sources.973423fe59d81b2e92440278 description:
The problem with ordinary possessions is provenance. Apparently one man carries a gold-plated pistol. Distinctive, impractical, interesting. Bring me Reshala's Golden TT and five tags level thirty-five or higher. A tag tells me what somebody was issued. A ridiculous gold pistol tells me what somebody chose to become.

A gold pistol is conspicuous enough to be foolish, yet someone carried one anyway. That choice interests me more than its price. If the stories about its owner are true, the object may say more about him than any formal record would.
sources.dc793bba6878ebbe565111ad description:
I think I've been looking at this backwards. A tag becomes interesting after its owner dies. Food, water and cigarettes only make sense because somebody expected to still be alive later. Bring me ten tags level thirty-six or higher and some ordinary supplies. I found Ross "Doc" Hunt in the notes. If Doc carried medicine, that tells me something. If he didn't, it tells me something else.

I have started writing down the food and small comforts people kept close. It feels intrusive in a different way from reading a tag, but perhaps more honest. These were things they expected to need tomorrow. I would like to preserve that fact alongside their names.
sources.adfc9ce5811d699712afe9f7 description:
We've discussed this. You're doing it again. Twenty tags, level twenty or above. I'll have them now, please. And before you ask, no, you're not getting another case. Read some of the names while you count. I don't care which ones. Actually, I do care. I simply can't explain why without sounding sentimental, so let's not.

I found another case tucked behind your bag when you came in. Do not look offended; I recognised the sound of the clasps. Bring twenty from the pile. We can at least make sure those names receive a place in the catalogue.
sources.b76e9343162ab87053e87365 description:
One. That's all I want. Level forty-one or above. Don't simply take the first in your case. Choose one, read the name, think about how long that person survived, then bring it to me. If it happens to say Giulio "Duke" Leone, don't get excited. I may already have had his tag. Or his brother's. Or neither. My notes are embarrassingly unclear on this point.

When I asked for twenty, I watched the objects disappear into a count. One person at a time may be slower, but it prevents that particular mistake. I have set aside two rifles, and yes, I made some adjustments despite everything I said about the hobby.
sources.768f4d12c1e2626be439a16d description:
I've been going through everything properly. There are a few loose ends. Five tags, level thirty-seven or higher. Five should be enough. Sooner would be preferable. Night Clerk, Bookkeeper and Red Ledger have all appeared in my peripheral notes now. I dislike that the market has developed a bookkeeping theme without consulting me.

There are pages in the ledger with figures carried over and no explanation of what the figures meant. I am revisiting them while I still can. Five records will close one of the gaps; the rest of the work is mine to do.
sources.b0f2dc120737ed220986b818 description:
Three more, level forty or above. That should settle this particular column. Bring me an energy drink too; I've been unusually tired lately. Don't make anything of it. I found Duke's name again last night. Then this morning I realised I'd been reading Edoardo Leone. I am beginning to understand why certainty is expensive.

The columns used to balance if I kept working at them. This one will not, though I have checked it three times. The drink is simply to keep me at the desk a little longer. I would rather finish a useful page than spend the evening explaining why I am tired.
sources.271dc61a970a7724a9bb53a0 description:
One tag, any one. Some water and a Max Energy too. And one of those stuffed BEAR toys. No particular reason. It looks comfortable. That is not a sentence I intend to discuss. I spent years trying to turn names like Duke, Strelok, Forester and all the rest into variables. They stubbornly remain people.

I have moved the chair closer to the window. The light is better there, and the collection looks different from a little distance. Bring the small things on the list. I would like to put the figures aside for an hour and talk when you return.
sources.f5ac229732049aea48fc9625 description:
I have one more page to finish before I put the ledger away. Bring me some paper and one tag level forty or above. I've begun sorting what I can leave behind and what ought to stay here. Nothing dramatic. I simply want it done properly. If Duke is alive, good. If he isn't, I hope someone read the name before selling the tag.

I have spent years writing down people I never met. It seems an odd omission that I have no proper record of the one person who kept coming back. The paper is for a new page. The tag will help me finish an older one. After that, there are a few final instructions to leave on the desk. I want you to be able to find things when I am no longer here to point them out.
sources.a7641df3fd811bc1ef2bcf19 description:
I need two bottles of beer. Yes, beer. Two. One for you and one for me. I've packed away the work, and I'd rather spend the time I have left sitting across from you than checking another column. Don't make a thing of it. I asked the Night Clerk whether this counts as closing the books. He said I should stop asking strangers for accounting metaphors.

The collection is arranged. I've made the decisions I kept putting off and written down where everything should go. There is a chair opposite mine that has ceased to be merely a place for visitors to wait. Bring two bottles, and we can leave the ledger closed. I would like our last conversation to begin with something other than a number.
sources.104094c6b6ff8c11b7d91153 description:
If you're reading this, I am gone. I knew we were close to the end when we shared that beer. The instructions are on the desk, and most of what I owned is yours. I have tried to leave as little ambiguity as possible. There isn't anybody else. I am sorry I could not tell you in person. The ledger still contains unresolved names. Duke Leone is one of them. Leave him unresolved. A person is allowed to be more than the answer to one of my questions.

There is a page on the desk explaining which things belong to you. The money and equipment are simple enough. The case is empty deliberately. What you put in it is your choice, as is what you remember of the people whose names passed through this room. I wrote this before our last visit. I hoped to finish everything while I could still speak to you, but I kept one final thought for this page.
sources.71a001f1a11ce00100000001 description: A supply chain is only as reliable as the person standing at the end of it. Bring me two MREs and two bottles of water. Nothing glamorous. If you can handle the boring work without losing half of it, I may open the better racks to you.
sources.71a001f1a11ce00100000002 description: One of my manifests has too many names still marked active. Bring me five PMC dogtags. I don't care which patch they wore. I need proof before I move restricted weapons off the books.
sources.71a001f1a11ce00100000003 description: The first controlled cabinet is armor and ammunition that attracts questions. Bring me ten dogtags from operators level fifteen or higher. If you're working at that level, I can justify moving serious inventory to your account.
sources.71a001f1a11ce00100000004 description: A scav crew has been hitting the Customs route I use to move protective equipment inland. Twelve of them should be enough to make the next convoy boring again. I like boring convoys.
sources.71a001f1a11ce00100000005 description: The public manifest is clean. The other ledger isn't. I need eight tags from operators level twenty-five or higher before I move the next rifle and ammunition allotment out of reserve.
sources.71a001f1a11ce00100000006 description: Last allocation. The stock in this shipment was never meant for open sale. Remove eight PMCs from the board and bring me twelve tags from level thirty or higher. Do that, and I'll stop pretending the black rack doesn't exist.
sources.67471f9c63d6ef6fe3ced898 description:
Hello soldier. I don't think we know eachother yet, people refer to me as Lotus. Word got around in the region that you seem to be reliable, is that true?

Knowing reliable and trustworthy people is important these days, especially for someone like me, after all business is everything here in Tarkov. How about you prove how reliable you are and if it is worth it to work with you, you will get some benefit from our work too so it's a win-win for both of us.

A few local bandits and other scum have made a few local areas in and around town less safe than usual, I want you to get rid of a them.

Good luck, we will stay in touch.
sources.67509b40ebc998b7d528d1a1 description:
Hey I heard you started working for Ragman, fantastic! Me and my team have been working together with him for some time, better to make good connections in a place where everyone is your enemy, right? Prepare yourself, lots of work is coming for you.

It's very likely that he will send you to the ULTRA shopping mall for most jobs, but don't be fooled, that place is extremely dangerous, we have to get you a bit prepared alright? Let's give you sample of what will be coming for you in that place, should we start? Great, there's a powerstation in the north-east of the mall, it controls the power for some of the stores and some other places, but I haven't gotten any intel for that yet.

Anyway, that station has an office, there should be some computers, electronic parts and some other stuff for sure. Find the office, then head to evac, a taxi driver is usually waiting directly outside that place ready to drive you to safety.
sources.67509c43d96ffa5a7187c025 description:
Alright, here's what's next.

Learning to fight inside the mall is crucial to your survival inside there, while you are inside there you're basically trapped. There are barely any places that let you get out of there without a fight so you'll need to be prepared, got it?

Take out anyone you see in that place. Let's not make this task easy however, make sure all your kills die to a headshot. Not too easy and not too difficult, for someone like you.

Anyway, good luck inside there!
sources.67509cb7f4536e3f9382009b description:
Hey listen up, I got something important where both of us could profit from, take a seat.

So, a mall of that size surely has some stores that sell something valuable, like jewelry or in this case... electronics. You probably noticed how valuable pc parts and electronics are here in Tarkov, especially in large quantities.

That's what we are after, the only thing you have to do for me now is to locate a few of these tech-stores, Arshavir gave me a list of four stores, locate them and then report back to me, simple right? Almost as simple as the payment for this job, I'll hear from you.
sources.67509d5ecf08e0fbf1764f36 description:
I got more work for you, so listen carefully.
One of my teams has been to the ULTRA mall at night recently, they visited the goshan supermarket and found massive amounts of food and drinks, somewhere in the northern part of the store. Install a camera somewhere nobody sees it, I wanna monitor who goes in and out of there, and what supplies they take with them.

After you're done with that part, check in the back of goshan where they usually unload cargo, you should see opened gates that should send you outside. Somewhere outside the south-exit there should be a few containers leaned against the fence, a blue and a green one, between them there is a passage that leads down onto another container loaded onto a truck.

Somewhere on the side of that road there should be more containers, and in one of the corners of the fences there should be a hole where you can extract from the location, can you remember that or do you want it written?
sources.67509e7057be1b2849ca4f57 description:
Some people might just have the urge to be better than everyone else, but some don't. But would you still wan't to know that feeling?

I have a test, for you. Cleaning the ULTRA mall could have two meanings, I assume you already know where I'm going with this, because I wouldn't ask you to literally "clean" the mall.

You see, your former colleagues, USEC or BEAR, whatever... They have been kinda getting on our nerves, I send out teams there pretty often and I don't wan't to risk the loss of any manpower, got it? I'd appreciate your help, but if you choose to help I must ask you to bring proof of your work, so don't forget to collect dogtags of your kills.
sources.674720e808312fa336c68ee6 description:
Alright listen up soldier. Been to the business center of Tarkov? I hope you are familiar with the place already because I need someone to go there and look for a fuel trailer. One of my guys told me his group saw a truck carrying fuel in the underground, not sure where that is supposed to be, so you are on your own there since I am against sending my guys down there again, nothing personal.

Don't forget to use one of these markers when you find it, I can lend you one but don't lose it.

And one more thing, don't forget to clear out the area a bit while you are at it, we don't want any third parties noticing our little operation here. Good luck soldier.
sources.6747235ed723d48c90cb644f description:
I'm always wondering how someone like you navigates around Tarkov, are you walking or something, wow...
You have some patience for sure. We do that differently, my guys usually use dirtbikes or certain off-road vehicles to navigate around Tarkov to check out all the areas or loot up. We got a small problem tho, our supply got kinda low and we are currently looking for some fuel source, help is appreciated.

If you can find us some fuel canisters that would help us out a lot. Also while you are looking for some, why don't you bring some Dryfuel aswell? I count on you soldier.
sources.674721e986f435b80234da65 description:
Okay so, in a warzone not just combat skills matter, you and a lot of other people are stuck here. You need more than guns and ammo, and by chance me and my guys need a few things. Nothing too crazy you would say but some of it won't be easy to find, which is why I ask you soldier.

Are you able to find basic household items like shampoo, soap and toilet paper. If you are skilled enough you might make some of them yourself in your hideout. Good luck!
sources.67472251414d587b8b36ba1f description:
So, wanna prove that you know where to find ammo? You know how important it is to know where to get your ammo. I might consider opening our stock of top tier ammo to you in the future, if you manage to bring the specific rounds to me of course... But that is something for later.

What I need from you now is to bring me a few ammo packs for 5.45x39mm ammo, bring me a few small boxes and a few large ones, that should be everything... for now.
sources.674722c60ad34fd118ec4c9e description:
Hello soldier, I got a job for you, are you interested? Good! Listen up, we are running kinda low on medical supplies and my guys struggled a bit with finding first aid kits and stuff like that. Can you help us out?

It would be great if you manage to aquire a few of every kind, small ones, big ones, extra big ones. Make sure to bring me some that werent used already! I want top quality first aid kits, understood? Off you go soldier, and good luck.
sources.674723bdd56b0c5b295bb6a1 description:
Hello soldier, are you doing alright? I hope so. I got something for you again. You see, I planned to stay in Tarkov for much shorter...

Recently a bunch of stuff broke down in our camp and my group are kinda busy with other things right now, so I can't just send them to bring all the materials. See where I am going with this? I want you to bring us batch of building supplies and a few electronis, I'll give you the whole list. 

I'm sure you will find enough, can I count on you?
sources.67472495fb91486f4fb89cb3 description:
Alright, now we know that you are able to take out bandits, but what about operators? After all these drunkards are not special, they are weak when alone, PMCs like you however are a real threat even when fighting them when they don't have any friends with them.
Lets put you to the test again soldier, take out some PMCs and take their dogtags with you, I want to see proof.

I got a lot of other things you can help me with but I need help from someone who knows how to fight, are you ready?
sources.6766e795bcba079415915b6b description:
People are on the hunt for special goods. Specifically people like you, PMCs, people who work with the local vendors a lot.

Someone called "Fence" always gave people the same challenge. You see, there are a ton of these souvenirs related to well known people around the globe and people have the task to find them all, one of each collectible.

If you are interested in having access to one of these new storage containers which are specifically made to keep these souvenirs, bring me three of these collectibles, don't worry about duplicates, just bring them and we can sell you as many as you need.
sources.677a55a0be2a8922dab9e040 description:
Good day, I hope you're feeling well. Interested in a little job?
Recently I have been contacted by another contractor, he specializes in military machinery, specifically vehicles from the cold-war era. You see, Tarkov is more than perfect for this guy since russia still has a bunch decade old equipment left and it's lying around everywhere.

Anyway, you wanna know what your task is, yeah? Alright alright, there should be two whole military trucks parked inside the old chemical factory, untouched, basically perfect condition for this matter. Since nobody would bother with getting these old timers out of that place.

Locate them, and place down markers, I can lend you two for this job but don't ask for new ones if you mess up! After you're done get out of there alive and report back to me, rest of the job shouldn't be our concern.
sources.67d769c37a074517a838b60b description:
Hey, there you are! I was wondering when you would show up again, listen I got something interesting.

Remember those trucks you located in the factory? Well they are all over Tarkov, I'm sure you know that, however...
Some of them were used to carry special Terragroup cargo. Somewhere in the customs zone you should find some of these vehicles, surely one or two of them were carrying some Terragroup stuff - Or they still do.

So, can you help me find these cargoes? I'm sure it will be worth the trouble, even if you don't find anything of interest.
sources.67e96d27ddd9ca3c4adbb5d4 description:
I got a clue!

You know that the factory workers lived in the dorms in the customs zone before the conflict, right? Well, so did some terragroup workers. I'd say that would be our next best guess, surely we find at least something.

The previous team I sent there checked every inch of the three-story building, not a trace of anything useful. Taking a look at the two-story dorm will be your job then, find some of the locked rooms, those should be the only important ones.

Look for some documents, laptops or briefcases - Anything that can help our "investigation", and don't forget to bring it to me once you found something, understood?
sources.67e972c039c5f34295a24265 description:
Hey, there's one more thing actually, while you were searching around the dorms, a few of my guys checked on the trucks that carry the shipments.

It turns out someone else was sniffing around the Terragroup cargoes! My team spotted some operators around these trucks, my guys took some photos of them and all the evidence leads me to believe that these operators are Therapist's people, ridiculous!

It's not in my interest to start some fight with more vendors, after all I'm already unpopular enough among some dealers. We gotta talk this out the civilized way, and I'm sure she would do it the same way, you know her better than me so you would know.

Contact her about the Terragroup "thing" we investigated, we'll see if we can work something out.
sources.67ea813bd8d2dc676746f53e description:
Hello again! I took a look at the shipment report that you stashed.

Seems like our USEC friends are involved... As if we didn't have enough problems already, but I know how we could take care of it. The rogue leaders roam around most of Tarkov, they get spotted pretty frequently near the scav base, which is not too far from the Terragroup shipments.

I suggest you look for some decent sniping spots, but that is entirely up to you, less risk when you take them out from a good position, you know. But you should absolutely use some form of sniper rifle to get rid of these guys, trust me, and bring some good ammo, their armor is not a joke.

Also it would be wise to take out all three of them at once, can you do that? And get the hell out there once you're done, don't forget that there are a ton of exfils around that place.
sources.67ee61b9f56b571ce703eec4 description:
Okay we waited like two hours now, I think it's time now. I actually got the next lead on these shipments. You see, the thing about the USECs did not give anything else that could help us much further, however a friend reached out to me over the radio.

We talked about these shipments, seems like me and Therapist weren't the only ones interested in them, but my friend wasn't that interested in those, anyway...
Since this friend wasn't interested, he decided to help us. He printed out some documents - Allegedly Terragroup related. One reads "0022" while the other one reads "0031", just so you know how they look like... roughly. He stashed both folders somewhere in the customs zone.

The first folder should be located somewhere in the Tarcone director's office, I think somewhere under the desk. The second folder should be hidden in one of the bunkhouses, right next to one of these Terragroup shipments actually. I suggest you grab them quickly before some scavs find them. Bring those folders to me.

When you finished that part of the job, you gotta check on the cargoes, make sure nobody swept the place clean. After all that is done, I'd say it's a good time to contact that friend I talked about.
sources.67efd429317486563c7ee2b2 description:
I decided it would be best to hand over copies of what is inside the folders to the BTR driver. You will be the courier, I hope that's fine for you? I will send someone to stash more copies where you found them before, just in case you lose the folders.

Next thing you're gonna do is visit a certain location - We might have tracked down another shipment. A big truck, somewhere near the old sawmill. Look for clear signs of Terragroup activity. Once you find that truck I suggest you mark it, and place cameras all around the cargo. If it's even there, so let's hope it is.

Sounds simple enough, right? Alright then, good luck out there, and make sure to get the hell out of there once you managed all that.
sources.67f107c6cd96ce08caca8b83 description:
We got it! Guess what the shipments contained, lots and lots of "medical supplies", Terragroup stimulants and resources to manufacture these drugs. Someone else will take care of securing the cargo and bringing them to a safer area.

Anyway, we will likely need to find some research notes, probably in some form of laboratory. It's much safer to check out some labs above ground, before we head down to the actual Terragroup laboratory, makes sense yeah? By the way, when I sent a team to the factory to take a look at the military trucks, they found a lab close to one of them, right next to the crashed helicopter. But they didn't have the time to do any further investigating. It's on the second floor, maybe we can find something there?

Well I guess that's your job now, head to the factory and find that lab, look for something useful, lab notes, journals, research notes, anything that could help. Got it? Alright, good luck then. I expect to see you soon, hopefully with those lab notes.
